exact_statement: For Bernoulli bond percolation on the two-sided nearest-neighbor integer line, p_c=1 and an infinite cluster exists almost surely at p_c. Consequently the hypothesis p_c<1 cannot be dropped from the recovered conjecture.
assumptions: Graph is Z with nearest-neighbor edges
source: Self-contained elementary boundary check; primary conjecture verification pending
proof_or_counterexample: For p<1, the probability that all n consecutive edges in either ray from a fixed vertex are open is p^n, which tends to zero. Hence each fixed vertex has a finite cluster almost surely; countably many vertices imply no infinite cluster. For p=1 all edges are open, so Z is one infinite cluster.

exact_statement: There is an infinite connected simple tree T of maximum degree 9 with p_c(T)=1/2 and theta_T(1/2)>=4/5. It is not quasi-transitive. Thus bounded degree and p_c<1 do not alone imply absence of infinite clusters at criticality.
assumptions: Vertices at level n-1 have 8 children when n is a power of two and 2 children otherwise
source: Independent elementary derivation in INDEPENDENT_DERIVATION.md, saved before any paired-proof read; no novelty claim
proof_or_counterexample: At p=1/2, M_n=E Z_n=4^(1+floor(log_2 n)); disjoint fresh offspring edges give E Z_n^2/M_n^2=1+(1-p) sum_{j<=n}1/M_j<=5/4 since the infinite block sum is 1/2. Cauchy-Schwarz and decreasing-event continuity imply theta>=4/5. For p<1/2, E Z_n<=4n^2(2p)^n tends to zero, also from any fixed descendant, proving p_c=1/2. The root is uniquely of degree 8, so all automorphisms fix it and there are infinitely many vertex orbits.

exact_statement: For the dyadic tree T of C1, the uniform-child ray measure on the host has I_(1/2)=5/4; with probability at least 4/5 its root critical component C is infinite, but almost surely every such component has p_c(C)=1 and admits no finite common-edge ray energy I_r for any r<1. Host finite ray energy therefore does not imply that a surviving critical component inherits finite ray energy under thinning.
assumptions: The exact dyadic tree of C1
Critical iid bond percolation at p=1/2
A ray measure is a Borel probability measure on infinite simple rays in the stated graph
I_r(mu)=E[r^(-K)] for the common undirected-edge count K of two independent rays
source: INDEPENDENT_DERIVATION.md; AUDIT_w435.md; independently reproduced conditional thinning and common-prefix calculations
proof_or_counterexample: Uniform rays have P(K>=n)=1/(2^n 4^(1+floor(log_2 n))). The tail formula gives I_(1/2)=1+(1/2)sum_n 4^(-1-floor(log_2 n))=5/4. Thinning the critical field by any rational r<1 produces iid bond parameter r/2< p_c(T), hence no infinite clusters. Conditioning, a countable rational intersection, and monotonicity give quenched p_c(C)=1 for every surviving component. Finite I_r would imply survival at r by the independently checked second-moment ray criterion, contradiction.
remaining_gap: Independent review pending; T is not quasi-transitive, so this is a refutation of unconditional inheritance, not the full quasi-transitive conjecture.
